classification.difficultyReason: Express the third fenced side as 500−2x, form the rectangular area quadratic, locate its maximum using symmetry, and interpret both dimensions. These are routine linked modelling procedures using the taught paddock method; the solution explicitly supplies the rectangular assumption.

content.prompt: A farmer has a straight fence along the boundary of his property. He wishes to fence a rectangular enclosure for a bull and has enough materials to erect 500 m of fence. What would be the dimensions of the largest possible paddock, assuming that he uses the existing boundary fence as one of its sides?

answer.short:
Assuming a rectangular paddock: $125\text{ m}$ perpendicular to the boundary fence and $250\text{ m}$ parallel to it.

The maximum occurs at the axis of symmetry of the quadratic area model.
answer.worked:
Assume the paddock is rectangular. Let $x$ metres be each side perpendicular to the boundary fence. The remaining fenced side is $(500-2x)$ metres, with $0<x<250$.
$$\begin{align*}A&=x(500-2x)\\A&=500x-2x^2\end{align*}$$
The area parabola opens downwards and has zeros at $x=0$ and $x=250$. Its maximum occurs at the midpoint:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{0+250}{2}\\x&=125\end{align*}$$
The side parallel to the boundary fence has length
$$\begin{align*}L&=500-2(125)\\L&=250\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
Thus the dimensions are $125\text{ m}$ perpendicular to the boundary fence and $250\text{ m}$ parallel to it.
